tasks.desc: Implement initial Python solution using closed-cycle formula (passed public samples but open-cycle case incorrect).
Derive corrected formula: all cycles require +1; impossible only when cycles exist and no buffer exists.

Update the Python solution to the corrected formula: count every directed cycle of length >=2 in the functional graph of changed appearing letters; a buffer exists iff not both S and T use all 26 letters; if cycles exist and no buffer, print -1, otherwise print changed_count + cycle_count.
Validate corrected solution on samples and edge cases: open cycle with incoming edge, multiple cycles, full 26-letter permutations, full S but T not full, acyclic chains, inconsistent mapping.

proposals: Implement the functional-graph closed-cycle counting method as the primary approach, with careful handling of appearing-only edges and buffer availability.
Implement a constructive 26-letter scheduler that resolves acyclic dependencies and uses buffers for cycles, to cross-check the formula on edge cases.
Build a small-alphabet BFS/DP oracle and random tester focused on open cycles, closed cycles, multiple cycles, unused targets, and full 26-letter permutations.
Develop a formal proof based on function composition, injectivity, and cycle dependencies to confirm the lower bound and the -1 condition.
Explore a merge-tree or reverse-splitting formulation as an independent alternative if the cycle-counting formula needs additional validation.
prev: Update the Python solution to the corrected formula: count every directed cycle of length >=2 in the functional graph of changed appearing letters; a buffer exists iff some letter is absent from S or some letter appears in S but not in T (equivalently, not both S and T use all 26 letters); if cycles exist and no buffer, print -1, otherwise print changed_count + cycle_count. Verify S=abcd, T=bcaa outputs 5.
